questions.q: Why was Reuben’s firstborn birthright given to his brother Joseph?
questions.a: His birthright was given to Joseph, son of Israel, because Reuben had defiled his father’s couch.

questions.q: From what son of Israel would a leader come?
questions.a: A leader would come from Israel’s son Judah.

questions.q: Who were the sons of Reuben?
questions.a: The sons of Reuben were Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.

questions.q: What happened to Beerah, the son of Baal?
questions.a: The king of Assyria took him into exile.

questions.q: Who were listed as heads among Beerah’s brothers?
questions.a: Jeiel was the head, and Zechariah was also listed among them.

questions.q: Where did some of Reuben’s descendants live to the east?
questions.a: They lived near the Euphrates River, at the edge of the wilderness, because their livestock had multiplied in the land of Gilead.

questions.q: When did the Reubenites make war with the Hagrites?
questions.a: They made war with the Hagrites in the days of Saul, defeated them, and lived in their tents throughout the eastern part of Gilead.

questions.q: Where did the sons of Gad live?
questions.a: The sons of Gad lived near the Reubenites in the land of Bashan, as far as Salecah.

questions.q: Who was the leader of the Gadites in Bashan?
questions.a: Joel was the head, Shapham was second, and Janai and Shaphat were also leaders in Bashan.
They lived in Gilead, in Bashan and its villages, and in all the pasturelands of Sharon to their borders.

questions.q: When were they all enrolled in the genealogy?
questions.a: They were all enrolled in the days of Jotham, king of Judah, and Jeroboam, king of Israel.

questions.q: How many trained soldiers did the Reubenites, Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh have?
questions.a: They had 44,760 soldiers trained for war, who carried shield and sword, and who drew the bow.

questions.q: Who did the Reubenites, Gadites, and half tribe of Manasseh make war with?
questions.a: They made war with the Hagrites and the people of Jetur, Naphish, and Nodab.
They were defeated because the Israelites cried out to God and put their trust in him, and God responded to them.

questions.q: What did they capture from the Hagrites?
questions.a: They captured 50,000 camels, 250,000 sheep, 2,000 donkeys, and 100,000 people.

questions.q: How long did the Israelites live in the land they took from the Hagrites?
questions.a: They lived there until their exile by the Assyrians.

questions.q: Where did the half tribe of Manasseh live with their families?
questions.a: They lived in the land of Bashan, as far as Baal Hermon, Senir, and Mount Hermon.

questions.q: Because the Reubenites, Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh were unfaithful to God, what did he do to them?
questions.a: God stirred up the king of Assyria and these tribes were taken into exile by Assyria.

commentary.text: —This chapter gives some account of the two tribes and a half seated on the east side of Jordan. They were made captives by the king of Assyria, because they had forsaken the Lord. Only two things are here recorded concerning these tribes. 1. They all shared in a victory. Happy is that people who live in harmony together, who assist each other against the common enemies of their souls, trusting in the Lord, and calling upon him. 2. They shared in captivity. They would have the best land, not considering that it lay most exposed. The desire of earthly objects draws to a distance from God's ordinances, and prepares men for destruction.
